cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 drink-sooner rationale gives A3 finish race; B4 already finished causes A5 fewest refills.

relationship.evidence: B4 ordinary second-cup decision changes A winning opportunity.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 actual victory into a new losing criterion.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea strength and B2 same pot make difference in milk explicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 stock praise adds no teacher-specific reason for the contest.
